entries.subject: Challener, Weiner Mansfield et al. (2025) Eigenspectra brightness-temperature maps at 25 wavelengths and their three regions
entries.finding: Shown as the 25-step Temperature lens, with the borders of the three regions drawn over it as thin lines as in the paper's Figure 1, read unchanged from the Zenodo deposit. Turned by this package's orbit and rotation, the deposited flux maps reproduce the deposited light curves; mirrored east-west they fit worse by a chi-squared of 384.8 over the 25 wavelengths.

entries.subject: The ThERESA 3D temperature grid of the same eclipse (8 wavelength bins)
entries.finding: The paper uses it only as a cross-check and says ThERESA struggled to match the emission features; its reduced chi-squared is 1.56 against Eigenspectra's 1.19. It is in the deposit but not drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper presents a 3D grid of this planet as its main result.

entries.subject: Hotspot temperature-pressure profiles retrieved with HyDRA and Pyrat Bay, with the whole-dayside HyDRA comparison (Figure 4)
entries.finding: Reopened when the user requested the deferred exoplanet profile chart. The Charts panel now compares the two hotspot fits with Coulombe et al. (2023)'s whole-dayside fit, using the deposited medians and 1-sigma credible bounds. Pressure units and column meanings are checked against archive documentation and independent values read from Figure 4. One prepared SVG uses the existing panel; the ring remains deferred separately.

entries.subject: Ring temperature-pressure retrievals from the same eclipse
entries.finding: The ring tables remain available in the 2025 deposit. The selected comparison uses the hotspot and whole dayside to keep the three medians and uncertainty bands legible in the shared panel; this does not exclude the ring data scientifically.
entries.revisitWhen: A separate ring comparison is requested and its retrieval assumptions are qualified.

entries.subject: Coulombe et al. (2023) broadband eclipse map of the same NIRISS eclipse
entries.finding: Two equally good solutions (a plateau and a peaked hotspot) and no deposited map file; the 2025 wavelength-resolved maps supersede it.
entries.revisitWhen: A map file of it is published.
